content.user_title: Validate Data with Pydantic and Zod
content.value_statement: APIs and forms often drift when validation rules are copied between layers. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical patterns for shared schemas, clear errors, and safer input handling.
actual_capabilities: Defines Pydantic create, update, output, pagination, and error response models.
Shows custom Pydantic validators for date parsing and age range checks.
Builds Zod schemas with inferred TypeScript types and cross-field validation.
Demonstrates React Hook Form integration with backend validation errors.
Provides string sanitization helpers for HTML stripping and length limits.
Documents schema sharing constants, contracts, and quality checks.
limitations: Examples focus on student records and must be adapted for other domains.
The sanitization helper is simple and recommends stronger libraries for HTML handling.
It does not implement authentication, authorization, or business rules.
It provides patterns and examples, not a runnable validation package.

use_cases.title: Design API request models
use_cases.description: Create clear Pydantic schemas for create, update, response, pagination, and validation error payloads.

use_cases.title: Validate frontend forms
use_cases.description: Use Zod and React Hook Form to validate inputs before submit and show field-level errors.

use_cases.title: Align frontend and backend contracts
use_cases.description: Document shared constraints so teams keep field names, limits, formats, and error behavior consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new API payload.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create Pydantic and Zod validation schemas for this form: [fields]. Include required fields, length limits, and clear error messages.

prompt_templates.title: Separate input and output models
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my entity fields and design separate create, update, and response validation models. Explain which fields belong in each model.

prompt_templates.title: Add cross-field validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Add validation rules that compare multiple fields for this workflow: [workflow]. Provide matching backend and frontend validation behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Audit validation coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these API and form fields for validation gaps. Identify missing constraints, unsafe assumptions, inconsistent errors, and sanitization needs.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for validation on a student creation form.
output_examples.output: The response lists required fields, email and phone formats, grade limits, date checks, and matching backend and frontend schema responsibilities.

output_examples.input: A team wants consistent validation errors across an API and React form.
output_examples.output: The response explains how to map backend validation details to form fields and keep user messages clear.

output_examples.input: A reviewer asks whether all external inputs are validated before database writes.
output_examples.output: The response provides a concise checklist covering schema coverage, length limits, sanitization, server-side validation, and response models.

best_practices: Validate every external input on the backend, even when the frontend also validates it.
Keep create, update, and output models separate to avoid leaking fields or accepting unsafe data.
Define shared constants for limits and formats so frontend and backend rules stay aligned.
anti_patterns: Do not trust client-only validation for database writes or privileged API actions.
Do not reuse database models directly as public request or response schemas.
Do not return vague validation errors when users need field-specific correction guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill generate complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides validation patterns, schemas, examples, and review guidance for existing applications.

faq.question: Can it help with both Python and TypeScript?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Pydantic for Python backends and Zod for TypeScript frontends.

faq.question: Does it replace backend validation with frontend validation?
faq.answer: No. It recommends backend validation for all external inputs and frontend validation for user experience.

faq.question: Can it handle custom business rules?
faq.answer: It can show validation patterns, but domain rules should stay in application services when they are not input constraints.

faq.question: Does it include sanitization guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for trimming, stripping HTML, length limits, and recursive database input cleanup.

faq.question: Is this skill safe for Claude Code and Codex workflows?
faq.answer: The reviewed content is documentation-focused. Static security hits were false positives from Markdown and TypeScript syntax.
